greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. We gather today in the presence of the Living God, seeking the light of His truth and the comfort of His presence.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to walk in the truth: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the light that shines in our darkness: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you promise to be with us until the end of the age: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
homily:
We begin today with a very small, very specific image: the act of planting. In the Gospel, Jesus speaks of the days of Noah and Lot, days when life seemed perfectly ordinary—eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building. These are the mundane, rhythmic actions of a human life. We plant a seed, we wait for the sun and the rain, we build a structure, we tend to our daily business. We do these things because we assume there will be a tomorrow. We do these things because we believe that our labor, our presence, and our future are anchored in the soil of this world. There is a profound, quiet dignity in this. It is the work of a life that is trying to grow, to reach, and to build something lasting.

I want you to hold onto this image: the planter. It is the image of a life that looks toward the horizon with hope. It is the image of Benjamin Vo. Think of his brilliant, curious mind, always coding, always building, always looking toward the next horizon—whether it was the architecture of the cloud, the logic of a new game, or the dream of his ‘con chim airlines.’ He was a boy who was constantly planting seeds of joy, seeds of curiosity, and seeds of love. He was a builder of connections. He was a boy who understood, in his own gentle way, that life is meant to be cultivated with care.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been five months since he went home to God. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know that the calendar moves forward, but the heart often stays in that room, in that moment, in that memory. We know the sharp, sudden ache that comes when you see something he would have loved—a new jet design, a complex math problem, a simple, silly joke—and the silence that follows is deafening. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the waves of sorrow that ambush you on a Tuesday morning. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s suffering. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus warns us: 'Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses it will save it.' This is the hinge of the whole mystery. We spend our lives trying to keep things exactly as they are—trying to hold onto the people we love, the time we have, the plans we made. We want to preserve the status quo. But the Gospel invites us to see that our true life is not found in the preservation of the past, but in the surrender to the future God has prepared. Benjamin, in his own way, lived this. Think of that remarkable moment when he unprompted told his parents he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for eternity. He was a boy who knew that the true wealth of life is not what we keep, but what we are willing to offer for the sake of those we love. That love is the seed that does not die; it is the seed that breaks open to become something infinitely greater.

Consider the first reading from the Second Letter of John: 'I rejoiced greatly to find some of your children walking in the truth just as we were commanded by the Father.' John is writing to a community that is struggling with deceivers, with those who want to complicate the simple, beautiful teaching of Christ. But he points back to the beginning: 'Let us love one another.' That is the truth. That is the commandment. Benjamin walked in that truth. He walked in the truth of his gentle, respectful spirit. He walked in the truth of his empathy for his family. He walked in the truth of his joy. When you think of him, do not look for the complexity of his illness or the mystery of his passing. Look for the truth of his life. Look for the way he smiled when he talked about his ‘con chim airlines.’ Look for the way he stood with his arm around Ryan in those holiday photos. That is the truth of Benjamin. That is the truth that remains.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

We hear in the Psalm: 'Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord! ... Within my heart I treasure your promise.' This is the turn of the heart. The promise of the Lord is not that we will never suffer, but that we will never be abandoned in our suffering. Benjamin is now resting in that promise. He is dwelling in the land of the living, and he is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected in the sight of God. He is not a memory; he is a living soul, fully alive in the love of God. He has found the destination he was searching for, and he is waiting for the rest of his family to arrive. He is the one who has already passed the test, as he said in your dream: 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết.' He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, he is waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is the one who has already passed the test. He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, cheeky grin, looking out toward an endless horizon. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity, holding the key. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may He let His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may He give you His peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin Vo and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light of Christ and find peace in the Father's home.
For all who are grieving, especially his parents and his brother Ryan, that God may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
[Chosen Lady:]
I rejoiced greatly to find some of your children walking in the truth
just as we were commanded by the Father.
But now, Lady, I ask you,
not as though I were writing a new commandment
but the one we have had from the beginning:
let us love one another.
For this is love, that we walk according to his commandments;
this is the commandment, as you heard from the beginning,
in which you should walk.Many deceivers have gone out into the world,
those who do not acknowledge Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh;
such is the deceitful one and the antichrist.
Look to yourselves that you do not lose what we worked for
but may receive a full recompense.
Anyone who is so “progressive”
as not to remain in the teaching of the Christ does not have God;
whoever remains in the teaching has the Father and the Son.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1b) Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
Blessed are they whose way is blameless,
who walk in the law of the LORD.
R. Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
Blessed are they who observe his decrees,
who seek him with all their heart.
R. Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
 With all my heart I seek you;
let me not stray from your commands.
R. Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
Within my heart I treasure your promise,
that I may not sin against you.
R. Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
Be good to your servant, that I may live
and keep your words.
R. Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
Open my eyes, that I may consider
the wonders of your law.
R. Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples:
“As it was in the days of Noah,
so it will be in the days of the Son of Man;
they were eating and drinking,
marrying and giving in marriage up to the day
that Noah entered the ark,
and the flood came and destroyed them all.
Similarly, as it was in the days of Lot:
they were eating, drinking, buying,
selling, planting, building;
on the day when Lot left Sodom,
fire and brimstone rained from the sky to destroy them all.
So it will be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, someone who is on the housetop
and whose belongings are in the house
must not go down to get them,
and likewise one in the field
must not return to what was left behind.
Remember the wife of Lot.
Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it,
but whoever loses it will save it.
I tell you, on that night there will be two people in one bed;
one will be taken, the other left.
And there will be two women grinding meal together;
one will be taken, the other left.” 
They said to him in reply, “Where, Lord?”
He said to them, “Where the body is,
there also the vultures will gather.”

pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
